__inputs.description: The InfluxDB 3 database ghchronicle writes to, queried with SQL.
__inputs.label: InfluxDB
__inputs.name: DS_INFLUXDB

description: Every metric GitHub will give about an account, kept with the date it happened. Collected by ghchronicle.

options.content: ghchronicle

panels.description: Public repositories of the account, and the current stars and forks of the selected ones, summed over the newest row of each repository rather than over every row in the range.

targets.rawSql: SELECT public_repos AS "Repositories" FROM gh_account WHERE $__timeFilter(time) ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1

SELECT SUM(stars) AS "Stars", SUM(forks) AS "Forks" FROM (SELECT repo, stars, forks FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_repo WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1)

panels.title: Repositories

panels.description: Page views, unique visitors and clones, summed over the dashboard range, so they move with the range picker. GitHub only keeps 14 days of traffic, so a range wider than that shows what was captured while it was still there.

targets.rawSql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'views' THEN count ELSE 0 END) AS "Views", SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'views' THEN uniques ELSE 0 END) AS "Unique visitors", SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'clones' THEN count ELSE 0 END) AS "Clones" FROM gh_traffic WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})

panels.title: Traffic in range

panels.description: Followers of the account and the accounts it follows, as of the last sweep; the two are different numbers and the second is usually much smaller. Then who sponsors the account and whom it sponsors.

targets.rawSql: SELECT followers AS "Followers", following AS "Following", sponsors AS "Sponsors", sponsoring AS "Sponsoring" FROM gh_account WHERE $__timeFilter(time) ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Community

panels.description: Contributions in the last year, the number behind the green squares on the profile; the days since the account was created; what it watches, what it has starred, its gists and its packages. Packages are counted from the package listing, the same rows the Packages table under Inventory lists: GraphQL reports zero packages for a personal account and is not what this reads.

targets.rawSql: SELECT calendar_total AS "Contributions" FROM gh_contributions_total WHERE $__timeFilter(time) ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1

SELECT account_age_days AS "Account age", watching AS "Watching", starred AS "Stars given", gists AS "Gists", packages AS "Packages" FROM gh_account WHERE $__timeFilter(time) ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Account

panels.description: Every pull request this account has had merged, anywhere, and every one it has reviewed, including in repositories it does not own; the public commits attributed to it, from the commit search index; the issues it opened; and the two numbers a sweep over one's own repositories cannot see at all, pull requests merged and comments left in other people's repositories. All counted by GitHub's own search rather than by adding up rows.

targets.rawSql: SELECT pulls_merged AS "Pull requests merged", pulls_reviewed AS "Pull requests reviewed", commits AS "Commits", issues_opened AS "Issues opened", pulls_merged_elsewhere AS "Merged elsewhere", commented_elsewhere AS "Comments elsewhere" FROM gh_account_total WHERE $__timeFilter(time) ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Since the account began

panels.description: The whole life of each repository in one row: not what happened in the dashboard range, but everything there has ever been. The repository picker holds every repository the account can see, its forks and its archived ones alongside its own, so a count here is over all of them until the picker is narrowed. Sorted by commits, a fork of a busy project outranks anything the account wrote, so the fork and archived flags are columns here and a click on either sorts by it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", MAX(commits) AS "Commits", MAX(fork) AS "Fork", MAX(archived) AS "Archived", MAX(pulls_merged) AS "Merged", MAX(issues) AS "Issues", MAX(releases) AS "Releases", MAX(stars) AS "Stars", MAX(branches) AS "Branches", MAX(tags) AS "Tags", MAX(url) AS "Link" FROM gh_repo_total WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Every repository, ever

panels.description: Each repository the account created, dated when it was created rather than when a sweep noticed it. Forks and private repositories are included, which is the point: those are exactly the ones a sweep with `include_forks` off never discovers. The contributions collection offers one trailing year of them at a time, so a fresh install sees a year here and the table reaches further back with every year the rows are kept. It names its own window rather than taking the dashboard's, so narrowing the range at the top of the page does not narrow this table.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", time AS "Created", fork AS "Fork", private AS "Private", url AS "Link" FROM gh_repo_created WHERE time > now() - INTERVAL '30 years' ORDER BY time DESC

panels.title: Repositories created

panels.description: `gh_repo_total` tags `archived` as a boolean stamped now, so eighteen archived repositories read as one undifferentiated fact. Dated at `archivedAt` the clear-outs are visible as the batches they were: eight of them within eight seconds of each other on one day. The default filter leaves archived repositories out of every collector, but not out of this table: the listing a sweep already pays for says which are archived, and each gets this one row from one query per `totals` sweep, so the table exists from the first sweep. An archived fork under the default fork rule is the one kind left out. A live repository produces no row, so counting the rows is counting the archive. It names its own window as well, so the dashboard's range leaves this table alone, and it takes no repository filter: the variable lists the repositories a sweep collects, and these are the ones it set aside.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", time AS "Archived", age_days_at_archive AS "Age at archive", url AS "Link" FROM gh_repo_archived WHERE time > now() - INTERVAL '30 years' ORDER BY time DESC

panels.title: Repositories archived

panels.description: The run listing's own total_count, which is every run the repository has ever had. The run walk sees the newest few hundred by design, so this is the only place the whole history is counted, and it is the answer InfluxDB 3 Core will not let a reader compute from the rows. A snapshot rewritten every sweep, so this is the newest value per repository rather than the sweeps added up. The ten repositories with the most runs are named; the rest are one bar called other.

targets.rawSql: SELECT "Repository", "Runs" FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN rn <= 10 THEN "Repository" ELSE 'other' END AS "Repository", SUM("Runs") AS "Runs", MIN(rn) AS o FROM (SELECT repo AS "Repository", runs AS "Runs", ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY runs DESC) AS rn FROM (SELECT repo, runs, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_workflow_run_total WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1) z GROUP BY 1) w ORDER BY o

panels.title: Workflow runs, ever

panels.description: Split by repository. GitHub serves a rolling 14-day window and it is rewritten on every sweep, so a gap means the collector was down for longer than that window. The eight repositories with the most in the range are named; the rest are `other`. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, CASE WHEN rk <= 8 THEN repo ELSE 'other' END AS series, SUM(v) AS views FROM (SELECT time, repo, v, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC, repo) AS rk FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, repo, SUM(count) AS v, SUM(SUM(count)) OVER (PARTITION BY repo) AS total FROM gh_traffic WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND kind = 'views' AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2) y) x GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(v) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Views over time

panels.description: Split by repository. The eight repositories with the most in the range are named; the rest are `other`. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, CASE WHEN rk <= 8 THEN repo ELSE 'other' END AS series, SUM(v) AS unique FROM (SELECT time, repo, v, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC, repo) AS rk FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, repo, SUM(uniques) AS v, SUM(SUM(uniques)) OVER (PARTITION BY repo) AS total FROM gh_traffic WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND kind = 'views' AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2) y) x GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(v) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Unique visitors over time

panels.description: Its own panel because continuous integration clones a repository thousands of times for every human visit, and on a shared axis the visits become a flat line at zero. The eight repositories with the most in the range are named; the rest are `other`. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, CASE WHEN rk <= 8 THEN repo ELSE 'other' END AS series, SUM(v) AS clones FROM (SELECT time, repo, v, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC, repo) AS rk FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, repo, SUM(count) AS v, SUM(SUM(count)) OVER (PARTITION BY repo) AS total FROM gh_traffic WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND kind = 'clones' AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2) y) x GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(v) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Clones over time

panels.description: Where the visitors came from over GitHub's trailing fourteen days. GitHub aggregates by host, not by URL, and attaches no dates, so this is the most recent snapshot rather than a sum over the selected range. The link opens the host; a search engine GitHub names without one has no link.

targets.rawSql: SELECT referrer AS "Referrer", SUM(count) AS "Views", SUM(uniques) AS "Unique", MAX(referrer_url) AS "Link" FROM (SELECT repo, referrer, count, uniques, referrer_url, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, referrer ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_traffic_referrer WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Top referrers

targets.rawSql: SELECT path AS "Path", SUM(count) AS "Views", SUM(uniques) AS "Unique", MAX(title) AS "Title", url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT repo, path, title, count, uniques, url, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, path ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_traffic_path WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY 1, 5 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.description: Clones divided by the people who made them. There are panels for clones and for views and none for the ratio, which is the only thing that separates adoption from machinery: one repository here is cloned seventy three times per unique cloner and viewed six hundred times in the same month.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'clones' THEN count ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'clones' THEN uniques ELSE 0 END), 0) AS "Clones each", SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'clones' THEN count ELSE 0 END) AS "Clones", SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'clones' THEN uniques ELSE 0 END) AS "Cloners", SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'views' THEN count ELSE 0 END) AS "Views", MAX(url) AS "Link" FROM gh_traffic WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Clone amplification

panels.description: Each star is dated by when it was given, recovered once per repository with a full walk of the stargazer list and kept from then on. The eight repositories that gained the most in the range are named; the rest are `other`. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, CASE WHEN rk <= 8 THEN repo ELSE 'other' END AS series, SUM(v) AS stars FROM (SELECT time, repo, v, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC, repo) AS rk FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, repo, SUM(1) AS v, SUM(SUM(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY repo) AS total FROM gh_star WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2) y) x GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(v) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Stars gained over time

panels.description: The star count as it climbed. The rows go all the way back to the first star, so widening the range shows more of the curve, and it holds its last value to the end of the range. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM gh_star WHERE time < $__timeFrom() AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) + SUM(n) OVER (ORDER BY time) AS "Stars" FROM (SELECT time, SUM(n) AS n FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, COUNT(*) AS n FROM gh_star WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 UNION ALL SELECT $__timeFrom(), 0 UNION ALL SELECT $__timeTo(), 0) a GROUP BY 1) x ORDER BY time

panels.title: Stars over time

panels.description: The twelve most starred; the rest are one bar called other.

targets.rawSql: SELECT "Repository", "Stars" FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN rn <= 12 THEN "Repository" ELSE 'other' END AS "Repository", SUM("Stars") AS "Stars", MIN(rn) AS o FROM (SELECT repo AS "Repository", stars AS "Stars", ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY stars DESC) AS rn FROM (SELECT repo, stars FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_repo WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1) WHERE stars > 0) z GROUP BY 1) w ORDER BY o

panels.title: Stars by repository

panels.description: The newest stargazers, one row each.

targets.rawSql: SELECT user AS "User", time AS "Starred at", repo AS "Repository", user_url AS "Link" FROM gh_star WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Recent stars

panels.description: The fork count as it climbed, rebuilt from each fork's own date the way the star curve is, so it reaches back to the first fork rather than to the day the collector started, and holds its last value to the end of the range. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM gh_fork WHERE time < $__timeFrom() AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) + SUM(n) OVER (ORDER BY time) AS "Forks" FROM (SELECT time, SUM(n) AS n FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, COUNT(*) AS n FROM gh_fork WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 UNION ALL SELECT $__timeFrom(), 0 UNION ALL SELECT $__timeTo(), 0) a GROUP BY 1) x ORDER BY time

panels.title: Forks over time

panels.description: The profile calendar, one bar per day at that day's own date. This is the only place the green squares exist as data.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, contributions AS "Contributions" FROM gh_contribution_day WHERE $__timeFilter(time) ORDER BY time

panels.title: Contributions over time

panels.description: The profile's green squares, as GitHub draws them: a column per week starting on Sunday, a row per weekday with Monday, Wednesday and Friday named as the profile names them, and a cell shaded by that day's own count. The four greens are GitHub's dark theme over the gray of a day with nothing, and the bands are the fifths of the busiest day of the year, which is the rule the profile page itself draws by: applied to GitHub's own counts it reproduced all 366 of its squares on 2026-09-14. The grid is the last year whatever range the dashboard is set to, because that is the only range this shape is legible at and the only one the profile has; the count itself, at any range, is the curve above. Three things the panel cannot copy from the page. The axis names the week each tick stands on, 5 Oct and 26 Oct, instead of naming a month over its first week: Grafana builds the ticks itself, one every few columns, so a month written there is printed twice as soon as the panel is wide, and the week it stands on never is. The cell is a fraction of the band its row gets, not ten pixels: the square is square at the size the panel is on the dashboard, and maximized, where the panel fills the screen, the same cells stretch into tall bars, so the grid is meant to be read in its place. And a cell's tooltip names the shade and the Sunday its column starts on rather than the day and the count: the panel colors by the value it shows, so the value has to be the shade, and a column is a week.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '7 days', time, TIMESTAMP '1970-01-04T00:00:00Z') AS time, SUM(CASE WHEN dow = 0 THEN level END) AS " ", SUM(CASE WHEN dow = 1 THEN level END) AS "Mon", SUM(CASE WHEN dow = 2 THEN level END) AS "  ", SUM(CASE WHEN dow = 3 THEN level END) AS "Wed", SUM(CASE WHEN dow = 4 THEN level END) AS "   ", SUM(CASE WHEN dow = 5 THEN level END) AS "Fri", SUM(CASE WHEN dow = 6 THEN level END) AS "    " FROM (SELECT time, date_part('dow', time) AS dow, CASE WHEN contributions = 0 THEN 0 WHEN contributions * 5 >= 3 * MAX(contributions) OVER () THEN 4 WHEN contributions * 5 >= 2 * MAX(contributions) OVER () THEN 3 WHEN contributions * 5 >= MAX(contributions) OVER () THEN 2 ELSE 1 END AS level FROM gh_contribution_day WHERE $__timeFilter(time)) d GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Contribution calendar

panels.description: The four kinds of contribution as shares of their sum over the last year, the mix the profile draws as a radar: commits, pull requests, issues and code review. The percentages are computed from the totals beside this, and the four add up to a hundred.

targets.rawSql: SELECT 100.0 * commits / (commits + pull_requests + issues + reviews) AS "Commits", 100.0 * pull_requests / (commits + pull_requests + issues + reviews) AS "Pull requests", 100.0 * issues / (commits + pull_requests + issues + reviews) AS "Issues", 100.0 * reviews / (commits + pull_requests + issues + reviews) AS "Code review" FROM gh_contributions_total WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND (commits + pull_requests + issues + reviews) > 0 ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Contribution mix (last year)

panels.description: One bar per week, at the Sunday the week starts on, which is how GitHub serves it and how the rows are stamped.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, SUM(commits) AS "All commits", SUM(owner_commits) AS "Own commits" FROM gh_commits_week WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Commits per week

panels.description: The last year, as the profile counts it: the same numbers GitHub shows under the contribution calendar.

targets.rawSql: SELECT commits AS "Commits", pull_requests AS "Pull requests", reviews AS "Reviews", issues AS "Issues", repositories AS "New repositories", restricted AS "Private" FROM gh_contributions_total WHERE $__timeFilter(time) ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Contribution totals

panels.description: The whole life of each repository, not the selected range: GitHub serves this distribution as a single snapshot.

targets.rawSql: SELECT hour AS "Hour", SUM(commits) AS "Commits" FROM (SELECT hour, commits, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, hour ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_commit_punchcard WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Commits by hour of day

targets.rawSql: SELECT weekday AS "Weekday", SUM(commits) AS "Commits" FROM (SELECT weekday, commits, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, weekday ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_commit_punchcard WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.description: Commits this account made in each repository over the last year, as the profile counts them. The rows include repositories this account does not own, so the name carries its owner in every store but this one, where the owner is dropped for width and the row is still identified by the whole name behind the column.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", commits AS "Commits", url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT repo, commits, url, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY full_name ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_contribution_repo WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND kind = 'commits') x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Commits by repository

panels.description: Every year, backfilled at one GraphQL point per year, reaching back to the day the account was created; the year in progress is here too, rewritten daily until it ends. A table rather than a chart because the past years sit outside any dashboard time range you would pick for the rest of the page.

targets.rawSql: SELECT year AS "Year", contributions AS "Contributions", commits AS "Commits", pull_requests AS "Pull requests", reviews AS "Reviews", issues AS "Issues", repositories AS "New repos" FROM gh_contribution_year WHERE time > now() - INTERVAL '30 years' ORDER BY year DESC

panels.title: Contributions by year

panels.description: Where the green came from, for the part of it that is commits. The eight repositories with the most commits in the range are named; the rest are `other`. "Contributions over time" at the top of this section counts issues, pull requests and reviews as well, so this stack sits under that curve rather than repeating it: a whole year of these days sums to `gh_contributions_total.commits`, the Commits of the totals above. The repositories include the private and third-party ones, which "Commits by repository" lists too, undated and unflagged. GraphQL caps the daily breakdown at a hundred repositories per window and, inside each, a hundred distinct commit days returned newest first, so a busier repository loses its oldest days silently: `gh_contribution_repo.commits` minus `commits_dated` is exactly how many commits never got a date. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, CASE WHEN rk <= 8 THEN full_name ELSE 'other' END AS series, SUM(v) AS commits FROM (SELECT time, full_name, v, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC, full_name) AS rk FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, full_name, SUM(commits) AS v, SUM(SUM(commits)) OVER (PARTITION BY full_name) AS total FROM gh_contribution_day_repo WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND commits > 0 GROUP BY 1, 2) y) x GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(v) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Commits by repository, dated

panels.description: Commits the public profile cannot see. A visitor sees none of the private half: a private repository is not on the profile at all, and its commits reach the green calendar only as the anonymous count the totals above call Private. The half somebody else owns is public work that no list of this account's repositories carries. Measured on this account, 8 of the 39 repositories with commits are private and 6 belong to somebody else. GraphQL caps the daily breakdown at a hundred repositories per window and, inside each, a hundred distinct commit days returned newest first, so a busier repository loses its oldest days silently: `gh_contribution_repo.commits` minus `commits_dated` is exactly how many commits never got a date.

targets.rawSql: SELECT CASE WHEN private = 'true' AND own = 'true' THEN 'Yours, private' WHEN private = 'true' THEN 'Somebody else''s, private' WHEN own = 'true' THEN 'Yours, public' ELSE 'Somebody else''s, public' END AS "Where", SUM(commits) AS "Commits" FROM gh_contribution_day_repo WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Commits the profile hides

panels.description: How much closed in the range and how long each took. Every duration is a median: half of what merged or closed took less than the number shown. Time to review by someone else is the wait before a person other than the author looked at a pull request, so review bots, which answer in seconds, and the author's own replies are left out; a range where nobody else reviewed anything reads No data, which is the honest answer and not the claim that nothing was reviewed. Lines per pull request is the median of added plus removed by a merged one.

matcher.options: Time to review by someone else

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Pull requests merged" FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND number IS NOT NULL AND state = 'MERGED'
SELECT approx_percentile_cont(seconds_to_merge, 0.5) AS "Time to merge" FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND state = 'MERGED'

SELECT approx_percentile_cont(seconds_to_first_human_review, 0.5) AS "Time to review by someone else" FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND seconds_to_first_human_review IS NOT NULL
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Issues closed" FROM gh_issue WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND number IS NOT NULL AND state = 'CLOSED'
SELECT approx_percentile_cont(seconds_to_close, 0.5) AS "Time to close an issue" FROM gh_issue WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND state = 'CLOSED'
SELECT approx_percentile_cont(churn, 0.5) AS "Lines per pull request" FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND state = 'MERGED'

panels.title: Merged and closed in range

panels.description: Merged and closed are dated at the moment it happened and stacked. Open that day is the line: how many were open on that day, which is a state and not an event, so it is not part of the stack. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, CASE WHEN state = 'MERGED' THEN 'Merged' WHEN state = 'CLOSED' THEN 'Closed' ELSE 'Open that day' END AS series, COUNT(DISTINCT number) AS pulls FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND number IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Pull requests over time

panels.description: One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, approx_percentile_cont(seconds_to_merge, 0.5) AS "Median", approx_percentile_cont(seconds_to_merge, 0.9) AS "90th percentile" FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND state = 'MERGED' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Time to merge over time

panels.description: Closed is dated at the moment it happened. Open that day is the line: how many were open on that day, a state rather than an event, so it is not stacked. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, CASE WHEN state = 'MERGED' THEN 'Merged' WHEN state = 'CLOSED' THEN 'Closed' ELSE 'Open that day' END AS series, COUNT(DISTINCT number) AS issues FROM gh_issue WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND number IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Issues over time

panels.description: Lines added plus removed per merged pull request. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, approx_percentile_cont(churn, 0.5) AS "Median lines changed" FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND state = 'MERGED' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Pull request size

targets.rawSql: SELECT number AS "Number", churn AS "Lines changed", repo AS "Repository", title AS "Title", time AS "Closed", author AS "Author", author_association AS "Association", label_names AS "Labels", changed_files AS "Files", reviews AS "Reviews", seconds_to_merge AS "Time to merge", url AS "Link" FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND number IS NOT NULL AND state = 'MERGED' ORDER BY churn DESC LIMIT 25
SELECT author AS "Author", COUNT(*) AS "Pull requests" FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND number IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 15

SELECT repo AS "Repository", COUNT(*) AS "Merged", approx_percentile_cont(seconds_to_merge, 0.5) AS "Time to merge", approx_percentile_cont(churn, 0.5) AS "Lines changed" FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND number IS NOT NULL AND state = 'MERGED' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.description: Who actually reviews, and how long a review waited. The count on a pull request cannot say whether the work is spread across people or resting on one, and an automated reviewer answering in seconds is visible here as a median rather than hidden in an average. A bot is marked as one, and the author's own replies on their pull request are one row called own pull request rather than a reviewer.

targets.rawSql: SELECT CASE WHEN self = 'true' THEN 'own pull request' WHEN bot = 'true' THEN reviewer || ' (bot)' ELSE reviewer END AS "Reviewer", COUNT(*) AS "Reviews", approx_percentile_cont(seconds_to_review, 0.5) AS "Wait" FROM gh_pull_request_review WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Reviewers

panels.description: One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, CASE WHEN self = 'true' THEN 'own pull request' WHEN bot = 'true' THEN reviewer || ' (bot)' ELSE reviewer END AS series, COUNT(*) AS reviews FROM gh_pull_request_review WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Reviews over time

panels.description: Time to merge only counts what merged. This is the other half: what is still open and how long it has been, which is the number that decides what to do next rather than describing what already happened. Each pull request is read from its newest row, so one that merged inside the range is not here any more.

targets.rawSql: SELECT number AS "Number", seconds_open AS "Open for", repo AS "Repository", title AS "Title", author AS "Author", label_names AS "Labels", comments AS "Comments", reviews AS "Reviews", url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, number ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_pull_request WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND number IS NOT NULL) x WHERE rn = 1 AND state = 'OPEN' ORDER BY seconds_open DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Open the longest

panels.description: The same question for issues: what is still open and for how long. Labels is what the issue was filed as, so an old one reads as a bug nobody fixed or a wish nobody granted. Each issue is read from its newest row, so one closed inside the range is not here any more.

targets.rawSql: SELECT number AS "Number", seconds_open AS "Open for", repo AS "Repository", author AS "Author", comments AS "Comments", label_names AS "Labels", url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, number ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_issue WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND number IS NOT NULL) x WHERE rn = 1 AND state = 'OPEN' ORDER BY seconds_open DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Open issues the longest

panels.description: Dated at the thread's first comment, which is when the objection was raised. Split by whether the reviewer is a bot: on this account the reviewers are review bots, and a backlog of bot threads reads differently from a backlog of human ones. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, CASE WHEN bot = 'true' THEN 'Bot' ELSE 'Human' END AS series, COUNT(*) AS threads FROM gh_review_thread WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Review threads over time

panels.description: A review thread is one objection, which GitHub keeps open until somebody resolves it. Threads is the whole conversation on that pull request; Unresolved, Outdated and Comments describe only what is still owed on it. An outdated unresolved thread is one the code has already moved past: debt nobody is going to pay and nobody has closed either.

targets.rawSql: SELECT number AS "Pull request", SUM(1 - resolved) AS "Unresolved", repo AS "Repository", COUNT(*) AS "Threads", SUM(outdated * (1 - resolved)) AS "Outdated", SUM(comments * (1 - resolved)) AS "Comments" FROM gh_review_thread WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: The review debt

panels.description: How many runs the range holds and how they ended. The success rate is the runs that succeeded as a share of the runs that succeeded or failed: a run canceled by a newer push under a concurrency group, or skipped by its own condition, decided nothing and is counted beside it as undecided rather than as a failure. The run duration is the median over the range and the queue wait is the time a job spent waiting for a runner, which only exists at job level, the run-level number folding the wait into the duration. Over the runs whose jobs were expanded, which is the newest runs of each sweep and, after a backfill, the ninety days GitHub keeps jobs for; not every run the run count includes. Last come the bytes the runs left behind, which are the artifacts the walk reached: GitHub lists thousands of them per repository and the walk stops at five hundred, so this is a floor wherever it did. "Artifact storage counted" below puts the two counts beside it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Workflow runs" FROM gh_workflow_run WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})

SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN conclusion = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN conclusion IN ('success', 'failure') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS "Success rate" FROM gh_workflow_run WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Undecided runs" FROM gh_workflow_run WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND conclusion IN ('cancelled', 'skipped')
SELECT approx_percentile_cont(duration_seconds, 0.5) AS "Run duration" FROM gh_workflow_run WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})
SELECT approx_percentile_cont(queued_seconds, 0.5) AS "Queue wait" FROM gh_workflow_job WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})

SELECT SUM(live_bytes) AS "Artifact storage walked" FROM (SELECT live_bytes, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_artifact_total WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1

SELECT SUM(size_bytes) AS "Actions cache" FROM (SELECT size_bytes, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_actions_cache WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1

panels.title: Runs in range

panels.description: One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, conclusion AS series, COUNT(*) AS runs FROM gh_workflow_run WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Runs by outcome over time

panels.description: One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, approx_percentile_cont(duration_seconds, 0.5) AS "Median", approx_percentile_cont(duration_seconds, 0.95) AS "95th percentile" FROM gh_workflow_run WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Run duration over time

panels.description: Over the runs whose jobs were expanded, which is the newest runs of each sweep and, after a backfill, the ninety days GitHub keeps jobs for; not every run the run count includes. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, approx_percentile_cont(queued_seconds, 0.5) AS "Median queue", MAX(queued_seconds) AS "Worst queue" FROM gh_workflow_job WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Queue wait over time

panels.description: Artifacts that have not expired, over the ones the walk reached, which is a floor on any repository with more than five hundred: "Artifact storage counted" further down has the counts that say which those are. GitHub deletes artifacts on their own schedule, which is why this falls without anyone doing anything. A reading taken at each sweep, so the curve starts the day the collector did: there is no history of it to rebuild. The eight repositories holding the most are named; the rest are `other`. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, CASE WHEN rk <= 8 THEN repo ELSE 'other' END AS series, SUM(live_bytes) AS bytes FROM (SELECT time, repo, live_bytes, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY newest DESC, repo) AS rk FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, repo, live_bytes, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY $__dateBin(time), repo ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn, FIRST_VALUE(live_bytes) OVER (PARTITION BY repo ORDER BY time DESC) AS newest FROM gh_artifact_total WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) y WHERE rn = 1) x GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(live_bytes) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Artifact storage over time

targets.rawSql: SELECT REPLACE(workflow, '.github/workflows/', '') AS "Workflow", COUNT(*) AS "Runs", r.repo AS "Repository", SUM(CASE WHEN conclusion <> 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Not successful", approx_percentile_cont(duration_seconds, 0.5) AS "Duration", MAX(w.url) AS "Link" FROM gh_workflow_run r LEFT JOIN (SELECT repo, path, MAX(url) AS url FROM gh_workflow WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2) w ON w.repo = r.repo AND w.path = r.workflow WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND r.repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 30

panels.description: Over the runs whose jobs were expanded, which is the newest runs of each sweep and, after a backfill, the ninety days GitHub keeps jobs for; not every run the run count includes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT job_name AS "Job", approx_percentile_cont(duration_seconds, 0.5) AS "Duration", repo AS "Repository", COUNT(*) AS "Times run", MAX(duration_seconds) AS "Worst" FROM gh_workflow_job WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 30

panels.title: Slowest jobs

panels.description: Over the runs whose jobs were expanded, which is the newest runs of each sweep and, after a backfill, the ninety days GitHub keeps jobs for; not every run the run count includes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step AS "Step", approx_percentile_cont(duration_seconds, 0.5) AS "Duration", job_name AS "Job", repo AS "Repository", COUNT(*) AS "Times run", MAX(duration_seconds) AS "Worst" FROM gh_workflow_step WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 3, 4 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 30

panels.title: Slowest steps

panels.description: Minutes that produced nothing. On the account this was written against, one repository burned 8,530 of its 15,111 minutes in a week on runs that failed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", SUM(CASE WHEN conclusion <> 'success' THEN duration_seconds ELSE 0 END) AS "Wasted", SUM(duration_seconds) AS "Total", 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN conclusion <> 'success' THEN duration_seconds ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(duration_seconds), 0) AS "Share" FROM gh_workflow_run WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Minutes spent on failed runs

panels.description: Not the ones that fail sometimes: the ones nobody has switched off. Two workflows here fail on every single run, 108 of 108 and 86 of 86.

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.repo AS "Repository", SUM(CASE WHEN conclusion <> 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Failures", workflow AS "Workflow", COUNT(*) AS "Runs", 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN conclusion <> 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS "Failure rate", MAX(w.url) AS "Link" FROM gh_workflow_run r LEFT JOIN (SELECT repo, path, MAX(url) AS url FROM gh_workflow WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2) w ON w.repo = r.repo AND w.path = r.workflow WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND r.repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 3 HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN conclusion <> 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 3 ORDER BY 5 DESC, 2 DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Workflows that keep failing

panels.description: Which step, not which job. This is the question that otherwise gets answered by reading job logs, and it comes from a table already collected. Over the runs whose jobs were expanded, which is the newest runs of each sweep and, after a backfill, the ninety days GitHub keeps jobs for; not every run the run count includes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step AS "Step", COUNT(*) AS "Failures", repo AS "Repository" FROM gh_workflow_step WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND conclusion = 'failure' GROUP BY 1, 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Steps that fail

panels.description: Sixty six of a hundred and thirteen declared workflows had not run in a week here. A workflow that never runs is either dead or waiting on a trigger that no longer fires, and nothing else in the dashboard would say so.

targets.rawSql: SELECT w.repo AS "Repository", w.workflow AS "Workflow", w.state AS "State", w.url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT DISTINCT repo, workflow, path, state, url FROM gh_workflow WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) w LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT repo, workflow FROM gh_workflow_run WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) r ON w.repo = r.repo AND w.path = r.workflow WHERE r.workflow IS NULL ORDER BY 1, 2

panels.title: Workflows that never ran

panels.description: What the workflows produced, at the resolution of one artifact. Seven hundred and ninety three artifacts and thirteen gigabytes in a single day here, which is where the storage bill comes from. The eight repositories producing the most in the range are named; the rest are `other`. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, CASE WHEN rk <= 8 THEN repo ELSE 'other' END AS series, SUM(v) AS bytes FROM (SELECT time, repo, v, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC, repo) AS rk FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, repo, SUM(size_bytes) AS v, SUM(SUM(size_bytes)) OVER (PARTITION BY repo) AS total FROM gh_artifact WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2) y) x GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(v) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Artifacts created over time

panels.description: Artifact storage, and how much of it was counted. Three counts, because the live size is on neither of the other two: Declared is GitHub's own total and counts the artifacts it has already expired, Walked is how far the page cap let the walk go, and Live is the artifacts still held among those, which is what the live size is the size of. When Walked is lower than Declared the live size is a floor rather than a total: here it is short by a factor of fifty six, and without these columns the tile above would say so nowhere.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", MAX(count) AS "Declared", MAX(walked) AS "Walked", MAX(live_count) AS "Live", MAX(live_bytes) AS "Live size" FROM gh_artifact_total WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Artifact storage counted

panels.description: How many commits landed in the window, how many lines each way, and what share carried a signature GitHub could verify. A commit with no signature at all is a different fact from one whose signature failed to verify, and both are counted separately in the chart below. The repository picker holds every repository the account can see, its forks and its archived ones alongside its own, so a count here is over all of them until the picker is narrowed. This panel keeps its own range of ninety days whatever the page is set to. Every commit is a row of its own in the store, and at about ten months of them the query is refused for opening too many files, which the reader would see as an empty panel rather than as an error.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Commits", SUM(additions) AS "Lines added", SUM(deletions) AS "Lines removed", 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN signature = 'VALID' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS "Signed commits" FROM gh_commit WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})

panels.title: Commits

panels.description: Additions above the axis, deletions below, per day. This is the answer to GitHub's own code frequency endpoint, which returns 202 with an empty body forever on a personal account. This panel keeps its own range of ninety days whatever the page is set to. Every commit is a row of its own in the store, and at about ten months of them the query is refused for opening too many files, which the reader would see as an empty panel rather than as an error. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, 'added' AS series, SUM(additions) AS lines FROM gh_commit WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 UNION ALL SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, 'removed' AS series, -SUM(deletions) AS lines FROM gh_commit WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Lines changed over time

panels.description: Pushes, branch creations and deletions, merges and force pushes, per hour. The only place a force push is recorded at all, and as perishable as traffic: a hundred entries covered twenty six hours here. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, activity AS series, SUM(events) AS n FROM gh_repo_activity WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Repository activity

panels.description: The twenty authors with the most commits in the window. The repository picker holds every repository the account can see, its forks and its archived ones alongside its own, so a count here is over all of them until the picker is narrowed. On an account with forks of busy projects the upstream authors are the top of this table, which is the honest answer to the question as asked: narrow the picker to read it as the account's own work. This panel keeps its own range of ninety days whatever the page is set to. Every commit is a row of its own in the store, and at about ten months of them the query is refused for opening too many files, which the reader would see as an empty panel rather than as an error.

targets.rawSql: SELECT author AS "Author", COUNT(*) AS "Commits", SUM(additions) AS "Added", SUM(deletions) AS "Removed", approx_percentile_cont(churn, 0.5) AS "Lines per commit" FROM gh_commit WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Commits by author

panels.description: This panel keeps its own range of ninety days whatever the page is set to. Every commit is a row of its own in the store, and at about ten months of them the query is refused for opening too many files, which the reader would see as an empty panel rather than as an error.

targets.rawSql: SELECT signature AS "Signature", COUNT(*) AS "Commits" FROM gh_commit WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Commits by signature

panels.description: Each force push, newest first.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", time AS "When", ref_name AS "Branch", actor AS "By" FROM gh_repo_activity WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND activity = 'force_push' ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Force pushes

panels.description: Whether the commit itself came out green. A workflow run that failed says a job failed, which is not the same claim: of fifty commits measured here, twenty seven left the default branch red. This panel keeps its own range of ninety days whatever the page is set to. Every commit is a row of its own in the store, and at about ten months of them the query is refused for opening too many files, which the reader would see as an empty panel rather than as an error. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, gate AS series, COUNT(*) AS commits FROM gh_commit WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND gate <> 'none' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Commits by gate state

panels.description: Everything Actions runs is already in the two sections above, in far more detail. These are the other gates: the code quality service, the dependency bot, the commit statuses an older integration still writes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT app AS "App", COUNT(*) AS "Runs", check AS "Check", SUM(failed) AS "Failed" FROM gh_commit_check WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Checks that are not Actions

panels.description: This is the panel that `oid`, `head_sha` and the gate state were stored for. Each of the three on its own says nothing; together they answer the question a red branch actually raises, which is which commit did it. This panel keeps its own range of ninety days whatever the page is set to. Every commit is a row of its own in the store, and at about ten months of them the query is refused for opening too many files, which the reader would see as an empty panel rather than as an error.

targets.rawSql: SELECT c.repo AS "Repository", c.time AS "When", c.author AS "Author", c.headline AS "Commit", r.failures AS "Failed runs", r.run_number AS "Run number", c.url AS "Link", r.url AS "Run" FROM (SELECT repo, author, time, oid, headline, url FROM gh_commit WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND gate = 'FAILURE') c JOIN (SELECT repo, head_sha, COUNT(*) AS failures, MAX(url) AS url, MAX(run_number) AS run_number FROM gh_workflow_run WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND conclusion <> 'success' GROUP BY 1, 2) r ON c.repo = r.repo AND c.oid = r.head_sha ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Commits behind a red branch

panels.description: The labels in use, per repository, and the link is that label's issue list. Only the labels something carries are collected, so a label nobody applied is not a row.

targets.rawSql: SELECT label AS "Label", used AS "Used", repo AS "Repository", issues AS "Issues", pull_requests AS "Pull requests", url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT repo, label, used, issues, pull_requests, url, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, label ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_label WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Labels

panels.description: The due date is collected as a field when a milestone has one, but it is not shown here: InfluxDB creates a column the first time it is written, so a query naming it fails outright on a database where no milestone ever had a due date.

targets.rawSql: SELECT milestone AS "Milestone", progress AS "Progress", repo AS "Repository", state AS "State", issues AS "Issues", pull_requests AS "Pull requests", url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, milestone ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_milestone WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Milestones

panels.description: Dated when each fork was created, which the fork count on a repository never says. The eight repositories that gained the most in the range are named; the rest are `other`. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, CASE WHEN rk <= 8 THEN repo ELSE 'other' END AS series, SUM(v) AS forks FROM (SELECT time, repo, v, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC, repo) AS rk FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, repo, SUM(1) AS v, SUM(SUM(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY repo) AS total FROM gh_fork WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2) y) x GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(v) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Forks gained over time

panels.description: Whether a fork was ever pushed to separates a derivative from a bookmark, which most forks are. Idle is the time since that push, counted from the row's own date, so it is right when the panel is drawn rather than when the last sweep ran.

targets.rawSql: SELECT by AS "By", time AS "Forked", repo AS "Repository", advanced AS "Pushed to", date_part('epoch', now() - time) - seconds_to_push AS "Idle", url AS "Link" FROM gh_fork WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Forks

panels.description: Discussions opened in the range, by category and whether they were answered.

targets.rawSql: SELECT category AS "Category", COUNT(*) AS "Discussions", CAST(has_answer AS INT) AS "Answered", AVG(comments) AS "Comments each", AVG(upvotes) AS "Upvotes each" FROM gh_discussion WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Discussions

panels.description: The newest fifty, whatever the range: an account has a handful, and a range of a month hid all but one of them. Answered reads n/a where the category takes no answer at all, an announcement or an idea.

targets.rawSql: SELECT title AS "Title", time AS "Opened", repo AS "Repository", category AS "Category", comments AS "Comments", CASE WHEN answerable = 'false' THEN NULL WHEN has_answer THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS "Answered", url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, number ORDER BY time DESC, comments DESC) AS rn FROM gh_discussion WHERE time > now() - INTERVAL '30 years' AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Latest discussions

panels.description: Labeled, closed, reopened, review requested, renamed: the moment something changed, which the state of an issue does not record. A reopening exists in no other measurement at all. The eight commonest in the range are named; the rest are `other`. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, CASE WHEN rk <= 8 THEN event ELSE 'other' END AS series, SUM(v) AS n FROM (SELECT time, event, v, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC, event) AS rk FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, event, SUM(events) AS v, SUM(SUM(events)) OVER (PARTITION BY event) AS total FROM gh_issue_event WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2) y) x GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(v) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Transitions over time

panels.description: Comments on issues and pull requests, in any repository. The ones outside this account are the half a sweep over one's own repositories cannot see.

targets.rawSql: SELECT full_name AS "Repository", COUNT(*) AS "Comments", MAX(CASE WHEN own = 'false' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Elsewhere" FROM gh_issue_comment WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Comments left

panels.description: Discussions are the one surface where the work is almost entirely in other people's repositories: gh_discussion sees three rows inside this account, and this sees sixty six across twenty six repositories.

targets.rawSql: SELECT full_name AS "Repository", SUM(answers) AS "Accepted answers", COUNT(*) AS "Comments", SUM(upvotes) AS "Upvotes" FROM gh_discussion_comment WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 3 DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Discussion answers

panels.description: Every comment this account left in a discussion of a repository it does not own, newest first and whatever the range; Accepted says whether the maintainer marked it the answer. The link opens the comment in its thread.

targets.rawSql: SELECT title AS "Title", time AS "When", full_name AS "Repository", answers AS "Accepted", url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY comment ORDER BY answers DESC) AS rn FROM gh_discussion_comment WHERE time > now() - INTERVAL '30 years' AND own = 'false') x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Answers elsewhere

panels.description: Webhooks fail silently. Nothing tells you a hook has been answering 403 for weeks except this.

targets.rawSql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN ok = 'false' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS value FROM gh_webhook_delivery WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})

panels.title: Webhook failure rate

panels.description: One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, code AS series, COUNT(*) AS n FROM gh_webhook_delivery WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Deliveries by status code

panels.description: Only the host is stored. The path of a webhook URL usually carries a secret. A retried delivery is a different fact from a first one that failed, and counting them together makes an endpoint look worse than it is.

targets.rawSql: SELECT host AS "Endpoint", SUM(CASE WHEN ok = 'false' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Failed", COUNT(*) AS "Deliveries", repo AS "Repository", SUM(CASE WHEN redelivery THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Retried", approx_percentile_cont(duration_seconds, 0.5) AS "Latency" FROM gh_webhook_delivery WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 4 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 3 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Webhook endpoints

panels.description: A 404 from branch protection does not mean unprotected: a repository can be governed entirely by rulesets, which that endpoint knows nothing about.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", ruleset AS "Ruleset", enforcement AS "Enforcement", target AS "Target", days_since_change AS "Last changed", url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, ruleset ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_ruleset WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 1, 2

panels.title: Rulesets

panels.description: A write key nobody has used in a year is a credential to remove.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", days_since_use AS "Unused for", key AS "Key", read_only AS "Read only" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, key ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_deploy_key WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Deploy keys

options.content:
### Failed job output

The last lines of every job that failed are collected too, but they are text
rather than measurements, so they go to a log store rather than here. With the
Loki sink enabled, this is the query:

```
{job="ghchronicle", kind="job_log"} |= "error"
```

Set `every.joblogs` to switch the collection on. GitHub deletes job logs after
ninety days and answers 410 afterwards, so there is no backfilling them: what
exists is what was captured while it was there.

Published to a Grafana that has a Loki datasource, with
`cmd/publish_dashboard -loki <datasource-uid>`, this panel shows those lines
instead of this note.

panels.description: The panel beside this one is built from deliveries, so a hook that has never delivered anything appears in it nowhere. This is the inventory: an active hook with no traffic is the interesting row. Hook is GitHub's id for it, the number in its settings page: GitHub names every webhook "web", so the name told nothing apart.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", host AS "Host", hook AS "Hook", active AS "Active", MAX(events) AS "Events subscribed" FROM (SELECT repo, host, hook, active, events, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, hook, host ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_webhook WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4 ORDER BY 1, 2

panels.title: Webhooks configured

panels.description: The same question the deploy keys table asks, about deployment targets: one environment here has not been touched in one thousand one hundred and seventy seven days.

targets.rawSql: SELECT environment AS "Environment", MIN(days_since_change) AS "Idle", repo AS "Repository", MAX(url) AS "Link" FROM gh_environment WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Environments

panels.description: Nothing else answers which branches were abandoned: GitHub's own branch list is ordered by name and keeps no history. The refs come back unordered and capped at a hundred per repository, so `gh_repo_total.branches` is the true count and is what makes the truncation visible. The repository picker holds every repository the account can see, its forks and its archived ones alongside its own, so a count here is over all of them until the picker is narrowed. Of the 1,208 branches in the picker when this was measured, 1,083 were a fork's; gh_branch carries no fork tag, so narrowing the picker is the only way to read this as the account's own branches.

targets.rawSql: SELECT branch AS "Branch", days_since_commit AS "Idle", repo AS "Repository", is_default AS "Default" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, branch ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_branch WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Stale branches

panels.description: What each branch protection enforces. `gh_repo_policy.branch_protection_rules` counts these and stops there, so a protection that is switched on and asks for nothing looks the same as one that blocks force pushes and demands three checks. Reviews is the number of required approvals, Threads whether every conversation must be resolved, and Checks how many status checks are required. Reviews is left empty rather than filled with a zero where GitHub reports no count at all, which is a different state from asking for none.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", pattern AS "Pattern", required_reviews AS "Reviews", CAST(requires_commit_signatures AS INT) AS "Signatures", CAST(requires_linear_history AS INT) AS "Linear", CAST(allows_force_pushes AS INT) AS "Force push", CAST(requires_conversation_resolution AS INT) AS "Threads", required_checks AS "Checks", url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, pattern ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_branch_protection WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 1, 2

panels.title: Branch protection rules

panels.description: Ruleset rules, and who may walk past them. The Rulesets panel above says a ruleset exists and is enforced. This says what it does and who it does not apply to: a ruleset reported ACTIVE with every actor on ALWAYS protects nobody, and neither that panel nor branch protection would ever say so. Always is counted over a page of five while Bypass actors is the exact total, so Sampled says how many were really read, and the comparison is sound only while the three agree.

targets.rawSql: SELECT rule AS "Rule", bypass_always AS "Always", repo AS "Repository", ruleset AS "Ruleset", bypass_actors AS "Bypass actors", bypass_sampled AS "Sampled" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, ruleset, rule ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_ruleset_rule WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 3, 4, 1

panels.title: Ruleset rules and bypasses

panels.description: Every saved version of every ruleset, dated the moment GitHub saved it. The Rulesets panel says a protection exists and how many days ago it last changed; this is the changelog that number summarizes, and it is the only record GitHub keeps of the moment a protection was switched off and back on. GitHub names the actor by type and id and not by login, so the row does too. Every store answers inside the dashboard range: a ruleset nobody has touched in the range is absent here, not unprotected.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ruleset AS "Ruleset", time AS "Date", repo AS "Repository", target AS "Target", actor_type AS "Actor", url AS "Link" FROM gh_ruleset_version WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 200

panels.title: Ruleset changes

panels.description: By environment. Dated at each deployment's own creation, not at the sweep that read it and not at its latest status: the status goes on moving for years afterwards, and the deployment happened once. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, environment AS series, COUNT(*) AS deployments FROM gh_deployment WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Deployments over time

panels.description: To status is the median time the deployment took to report one; Live for the median time it stayed the current one. They are the same subtraction against two different meanings, so each keeps its own field and neither is written over the other. The pending rows are kept on purpose: one deployment on this account has been held at an approval for seventy four days, and a filter that hid the states that are not terminal would delete the most interesting row.

targets.rawSql: SELECT environment AS "Environment", COUNT(*) AS "Deployments", repo AS "Repository", approx_percentile_cont(seconds_to_status, 0.5) AS "To status", approx_percentile_cont(seconds_live, 0.5) AS "Live for", SUM(CASE WHEN success THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Successes", SUM(CASE WHEN outcome = 'pending' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Pending", MAX(url) AS "Link", MAX(environment_url) AS "Live" FROM gh_deployment WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Deployments by environment

panels.description: Release asset downloads, counted by GitHub since each release was published, and how many releases have been downloaded at all, as of the newest reading of each.

targets.rawSql: SELECT SUM(downloads) AS "Total" FROM (SELECT downloads, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, tag ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_release WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1

SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Releases" FROM (SELECT repo, tag, downloads, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, tag ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_release WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 AND downloads > 0

panels.title: Downloads

panels.description: The twelve most downloaded releases. A click on a bar opens the release page.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo || ' ' || tag AS "Release", downloads AS "Downloads", url AS "Page" FROM (SELECT repo, tag, downloads, url, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, tag ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_release WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 AND downloads > 0 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 12

panels.title: Downloads by release

panels.description: Download fetches the file itself, which is what an asset's url is; the asset's name opens the release page it was published on.

targets.rawSql: SELECT a.asset AS "Asset", a.downloads AS "Downloads", a.tag AS "Tag", a.repo AS "Repository", a.size_bytes AS "Size", a.url AS "Download", r.url AS "Link" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, tag, asset ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_release_asset WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) a LEFT JOIN (SELECT repo, tag, url, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, tag ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_release WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) r ON r.repo = a.repo AND r.tag = a.tag AND r.rn = 1 WHERE a.rn = 1 ORDER BY a.downloads DESC LIMIT 40

panels.title: Release assets

panels.description: The counter is cumulative, so what matters is the difference across the range. A day of it here: ninety seven per cent of the downloads are one Linux binary and its checksum file, which is an installer rather than a person.

targets.rawSql: SELECT asset AS "Asset", MAX(downloads) - MIN(downloads) AS "Gained", MAX(downloads) AS "Total", tag AS "Tag", repo AS "Repository", MAX(url) AS "Download" FROM gh_release_asset WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 4, 5 HAVING MAX(downloads) > MIN(downloads) ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Downloads gained

panels.description: Alerts still open, from the newest reading of each repository. Both are colored by the same thresholds, so one value can be green beside a red one.

targets.rawSql: SELECT SUM(open) AS "Dependabot" FROM (SELECT open, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, severity, ecosystem ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_dependabot_alert WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1

SELECT SUM(open) AS "Code scanning" FROM (SELECT open, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, severity, tool ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_code_scanning_alert WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1

panels.title: Open alerts

targets.rawSql: SELECT severity AS "Severity", SUM(open) AS "Open alerts" FROM (SELECT severity, open, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, severity, ecosystem ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_dependabot_alert WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

SELECT ecosystem AS "Ecosystem", SUM(open) AS "Open alerts" FROM (SELECT ecosystem, open, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, severity, ecosystem ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_dependabot_alert WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.description: The open count per severity, added up across repositories and ecosystems from the newest reading of each. A reading taken at each sweep, so the curve starts the day the collector did. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, severity AS series, SUM(open) AS alerts FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, severity, open, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY $__dateBin(time), repo, severity, ecosystem ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_dependabot_alert WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Open alerts over time

panels.description: Recorded explicitly, so a repository with the feature switched off is distinguishable from one with no alerts.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", feature AS "Feature", MAX(CAST(enabled AS INT)) AS "Enabled", MAX(open_alerts) AS "Open alerts", url AS "Link" FROM gh_security_feature WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2, 5 ORDER BY 1, 2

panels.title: Security features

panels.description: That the scan ran at all, which the alert list cannot tell you. GitHub prunes these, so they only exist if they were captured. The eight tools that ran the most in the range are named; the rest are `other`. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, CASE WHEN rk <= 8 THEN tool ELSE 'other' END AS series, SUM(v) AS analyses FROM (SELECT time, tool, v, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC, tool) AS rk FROM (SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, tool, SUM(1) AS v, SUM(SUM(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY tool) AS total FROM gh_code_scanning_analysis WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 2) y) x GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(v) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Code scanning runs

panels.description: Code scanning alerts that were fixed or dismissed, and how long each severity stayed open. The list was always downloaded whole and these dates thrown away, so before this only the open count existed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT severity AS "Severity", COUNT(*) AS "Alerts", approx_percentile_cont(seconds_to_resolve, 0.5) AS "Time to resolve" FROM gh_code_scanning_alert_item WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND seconds_to_resolve IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Scanning alerts resolved

panels.description: Dependabot alerts that were fixed or dismissed, newest first, with the advisory each one was and how long it stayed open. The score is there because the word rounds it away: one alert in the measured account scores 9.3 under a word whose mean is 6.1. It is the v4 score where the advisory carries one.

targets.rawSql: SELECT package AS "Package", time AS "Raised", repo AS "Repository", severity AS "Severity", summary AS "Advisory", COALESCE(cvss_v4, cvss) AS "CVSS", dismissed_reason AS "Dismissed", seconds_to_resolve AS "Time to resolve", url AS "Link" FROM gh_dependabot_alert_item WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND seconds_to_resolve IS NOT NULL ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Time to resolve an alert

panels.description: The panel beside this one says the scan ran. This says what it found, which is what explains a jump in the alert count: one tool here returns sixty three results in three runs and another fifty two in nine hundred and fifty three.

targets.rawSql: SELECT tool AS "Tool", SUM(results) AS "Results", repo AS "Repository", COUNT(*) AS "Runs", MAX(rules) AS "Rules" FROM gh_code_scanning_analysis WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) GROUP BY 1, 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Scan results by tool

panels.description: The two counts at the top of the section, as the rows they are made of, whatever the dashboard range: an alert is listed while it is open, however long ago it was raised. A Dependabot alert names its package and advisory, a code scanning alert its rule and tool. Open for is counted from the row's own date to now, so it is right when the panel is drawn rather than when the last sweep ran. The link opens the alert, which GitHub shows to the owner alone.

targets.rawSql: SELECT package AS "What", time AS "Raised", 'dependabot' AS "Kind", repo AS "Repository", severity AS "Severity", summary AS "Detail", date_part('epoch', now() - time) AS "Open for", url AS "Link" FROM gh_dependabot_alert_item WHERE time > now() - INTERVAL '30 years' AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND alert_state = 'open' UNION ALL SELECT rule AS "What", time AS "Raised", 'code scanning' AS "Kind", repo AS "Repository", severity AS "Severity", tool AS "Detail", date_part('epoch', now() - time) AS "Open for", url AS "Link" FROM gh_code_scanning_alert_item WHERE time > now() - INTERVAL '30 years' AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote}) AND alert_state = 'open' ORDER BY 2 LIMIT 25

panels.title: Oldest open alerts

panels.description: What the repository itself says about the five security_and_analysis keys, which have three states and not two: `unavailable` is GitHub omitting the whole block on a private repository, and that is not `disabled`. Read it against the Security features panel above, where one is the repository's own setting and the other is whether the listing answered at all: a row where the two disagree is the row worth reading.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", setting AS "Setting", status AS "Status", CAST(enabled AS INT) AS "Enabled" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, setting ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_security_setting WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 4, 1, 2

panels.title: Security settings

panels.description: GitHub's own default setup, and nothing else. A repository can answer not-configured here and still run CodeQL from a workflow it wrote itself, which the Code scanning runs panel above sees and this one does not. In not-configured, `languages` is what GitHub detected in the repository, not what anything analyzed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", state AS "State", query_suite AS "Query suite", schedule AS "Schedule", languages AS "Languages", days_since_change AS "Last changed" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_code_scanning_setup WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Default code scanning setup

panels.description: The default permissions of GITHUB_TOKEN, which is what a compromised action inherits. `write` beside can-approve-pull-requests on is the supply-chain row: that workflow can push a change and approve it. `read` means a workflow cannot push at all.

targets.rawSql: SELECT repo AS "Repository", permissions AS "Permissions", CAST(can_approve_pr AS INT) AS "Can approve pull requests" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_actions_policy WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Workflow token permissions

panels.description: Secrets, and when they were last rotated. Both numbers or the panel says nothing: days_since_rotation equals age_days until somebody rotates the secret, so the gap between the two columns is the only evidence a credential was ever replaced. The names are public already, written in the workflow that reads them; the values never leave GitHub.

targets.rawSql: SELECT secret AS "Secret", days_since_rotation AS "Last rotated", age_days AS "Age", repo AS "Repository", kind AS "Kind" FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repo, kind, secret ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM gh_secret WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND repo IN (${repo:singlequote})) x WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Secret rotation

panels.description: What the usage would have cost at list price, what the plan covered, and what was actually billed, which is not always zero because the monthly credit shows up there. Then the runner minutes behind it, as a count rather than a duration: these are minutes of machine time, not elapsed time, and a "2.3 days" would be a lie.

targets.rawSql: SELECT SUM(gross) AS "Gross", SUM(discount) AS "Covered by the plan", SUM(net) AS "Actually billed", SUM(CASE WHEN unit = 'Minutes' THEN quantity ELSE 0 END) AS "Actions minutes" FROM gh_billing_usage WHERE $__timeFilter(time)

panels.title: Spend in range

panels.description: Gross cost per day. One bar is one bucket, and the bucket widens with the range: a day over a month, a week over a year.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__dateBin(time) AS time, product AS series, SUM(gross) AS cost FROM gh_billing_usage WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Cost over time by product
